findings.evidence: Neither SOURCE 1 (page), SOURCE 2 (app.js), nor SOURCE 3 (README) publishes a release identifier for the board. README describes a fixed set of 40 tasks/10 domains (badges 'Tasks-40', domains table, '40 tasks total') and news entries, but no maintainer-published version number for the board that '40-tasks' could copy. Per c2, 'published' requires the maintainer to publish a release identifier that the row's version copies; a page publishing none supports 'snapshot', and 'snapshot' is a mismatch only when a release identifier is published.
findings.repair: Change version_status from "published" to "snapshot" (with version as the dated snapshot identity per registry convention), or supply primary evidence of a maintainer-published release identifier for this board that "40-tasks" transcribes.

uncertainties: Row claims the page's default view is Pass@1 with Pass@5 taking the best of five attempts; README (SOURCE 3) only records that Pass@5 leaderboard results were added 2026-07-01, which does not explicitly establish the default view. Not a numeric mismatch; noted as unverifiable from the excerpt.

Row claims coverage on 2026-09-21 was 33–40 of 40 tasks with mean cost per task kept in each row's protocol; these per-row details are not in the packet and were not judged as claims of fresh measurement.

Row's claims that page says '100 = surpasses it' (confirmed in SOURCE 1 frontier text) and README '70+' (confirmed in SOURCE 3) were verified; other guard clauses (exact 40 task ids, leaderboard.json keys) cannot be fully verified from the bounded excerpts, but neither source contradicts them.
Hash integrity, transport and qualification checks are owner-executed; I cannot recompute SHA-256 values, including per-row binding hashes or output_sha256 in the producer receipt.
